clue.text: Poet reportedly cheated

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the poet's name is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: John Donne, the English metaphysical poet

explanation.surface: A rumour that some poet was a cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: To be done is slang for being swindled or conned, so it can replace cheated.

clue.text: Interference in stable

definitions.meaning: crackle or noise disturbing a radio or TV signal

explanation.definitionFit: Static is both electrical noise on a broadcast and an adjective for something fixed and unmoving.

clue.text: Party in power, lacking leadership

indicators.note: the word for power loses its leading letter, its first one

parts.note: steam is motive power, as in a steam engine

explanation.surface: A political party in government that has no leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party in power' reads as one phrase, but 'Party' alone is the definition and 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A team is a group working together, as is a party, such as a search party.

clue.text: Old train company accommodating woman as standard

indicators.note: accommodating means holding a guest inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former UK national railway
Anne is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A former railway firm putting up a female employee as a matter of course.
explanation.walkthrough: BR stands for British Rail, the state-run railway the UK had until the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag carried in procession, which is what a banner is.

clue.text: Fried noodles cold — who cooked? Me, at home

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: cooked means the word who is prepared into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: Someone asks who made the cold noodles, and answers that they did, at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Chow mein is the Chinese-style dish of stir-fried noodles.

clue.text: Diplomat, a male, so sad, drunk in pub

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the word for pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: drunk means the words so sad are reeling into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An envoy, a man so miserable he is getting drunk in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so sad, drunk' reads as a description of the diplomat's state, but 'drunk' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambassador is a senior diplomat representing a country abroad.

clue.text: Wine expert? Lightweight!

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
able means skilled or expert

explanation.surface: Mocking a supposed wine connoisseur as a weakling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lightweight!' seems an insult; it is the definition, meaning easy to carry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something portable is light enough to be carried about easily.

clue.text: Nightbird seen in Crosby making deliveries

indicators.note: seen in puts the bird inside the singer's first name

parts.note: Bing Crosby, the American singer
an owl is a bird active at night

explanation.surface: An owl spotted in the town of Crosby while a delivery round goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosby looks like a place; it is the singer Bing Crosby.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, bowling is sending down deliveries of the ball to the batsman.

clue.text: Familiar with a hospital shown in book

indicators.note: shown in places the hospital letter inside the word for book

parts.note: a tome is a large book
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone familiar with a hospital that features in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at home with something is to be comfortable and well acquainted with it.

clue.text: First round with present

parts.note: best means first or top
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Winning the first round and receiving a present for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' is a verb here, not a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestow is to give or confer, as when presenting an award.

clue.text: Grown-up lads use four-letter words, such as vest, suit, and ties!

definitions.text: such as vest, suit, and ties

parts.note: lads who have grown up are men
to use four-letter words is to curse, to swear

explanation.surface: Grown lads cursing, with a jokey list that pretends vest, suit and ties are swear words.
explanation.walkthrough: Vest, suit and ties are all four-letter words, so the list seems to illustrate the swearing; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Vests, suits and ties are examples of clothing for men.

clue.text: Such a dismissal may be given by a drill-sergeant

definitions.text: Such a dismissal may be given by a drill-sergeant

parts.words: Such a dismissal may be given by a drill-sergeant
parts.note: a drill-sergeant gives orders to march, and the phrase for being sacked is to be given these

explanation.definitionFit: Being given your marching orders is an idiom for being dismissed or told to leave, and a drill-sergeant literally orders marching.

clue.text: Not friendly towards others, worker is one in pub blowing top

parts.note: an ant is a worker insect
taken as written

indicators.note: in puts the numeral inside what remains of the pub
blowing top means the word for pub loses its top, its first letter

parts.note: the local is one's neighbourhood pub
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An unfriendly worker who loses his temper in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing top' looks like losing one's temper; it takes the L from LOCAL, leaving OCAL, and 'in' puts I inside it. 'The local' is British for one's nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Antisocial describes someone who avoids company or behaves badly towards other people.

clue.text: Greek with thousand pounds

parts.note: and means together with

explanation.surface: A Greek person with a thousand pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars.

clue.text: Finish work on stone

indicators.note: on means the word for work comes next to the stone

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Telling a mason to put the last touches to some stonework.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds, abbreviated ST.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop is to finish or come to an end.

clue.text: Make light of theatrical piece, blue

parts.note: a play is a piece for the theatre
blue means sad or depressed, down

explanation.surface: Mocking a stage work that is a bit risqué.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' suggests a colour or smut; here it means low in spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: To play down something is to minimise its importance.

clue.text: Crook who sneaks in King George mug

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George
a mug is a fool, an ass

explanation.surface: A thief slipping into the King George to steal a mug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King George' reads as a pub name; it is GR, Georgius Rex. 'Grass' is British slang for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: A grass is a criminal who informs on others to the police, a crook who tells tales.

clue.text: Figure of female makes one stop broadcasting

parts.note: a sign is a figure or symbol

explanation.surface: A woman's figure making a man halt a broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign off is to end a broadcast or message.

clue.text: With nothing on brownish-grey horse, backed last in race

indicators.note: backed means the horse's word runs backwards

parts.note: a dun is a horse of greyish-brown colour

indicators.note: last in takes the final letter of the word race

explanation.surface: A punter backs a dun horse which finishes last, wearing no rider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' sounds like betting on a horse; it turns DUN into NUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone nude has no clothes on at all.

clue.text: Long-haired right-winger swallowing setter's yarn

indicators.note: swallowing means the long-haired Tory takes the dog's word inside

parts.note: shaggy means having long, rough hair
a Tory is a British Conservative, a right-winger
a setter is a breed of dog, and the possessive gives an S

explanation.surface: A long-haired Conservative taking in the crossword setter's tall tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter's' hints at the compiler; it is a breed of dog. 'Yarn' means a story, not wool.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaggy dog story is a long, rambling yarn with a pointless ending.

clue.text: Outlying farm, good place to practise shooting

parts.note: a range is a place for target practice

explanation.surface: A remote farm that makes a fine spot for target shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: A grange is a country house with farm buildings, originally an outlying farm of a monastery.

clue.text: Attempt to secure one pound for a hat

indicators.note: to secure means the attempt holds the other pieces fast inside it

parts.note: a try is an attempt
I is the Roman numeral one
LB is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: Trying to buy a hat for one pound.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilby is a soft felt hat with a dented crown.

clue.text: Form of pollution in sewer — CIA involved initially

indicators.note: initially means the tangled letters come at the start, before the sewer
involved means the letters of the agency are tangled up

parts.note: taken as written
a drain is a sewer

explanation.surface: The CIA implicated in contaminating a sewer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in sewer' looks part of the definition, but 'in' is a link word. 'involved' turns CIA into ACI.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid rain is precipitation made acidic by industrial emissions, a well-known pollutant.

clue.text: River's in the heart of Sweden, I learned

indicators.note: in the heart of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone reports a river they learned about in central Sweden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River's' stands for 'River is', with the 's' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is the great river flowing through Egypt.

clue.text: Bird, duck, on turbulent Loire

indicators.note: on places the jumbled river after the duck

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, O

indicators.note: turbulent means the river's letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A duck bobbing on the choppy waters of the Loire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' is the cricket zero, O; 'turbulent' makes RIOLE from LOIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: An oriole is a brightly coloured songbird, often yellow and black.

clue.text: Welsh town fellow's eschewed dressing

indicators.note: eschewed means the fellow's letter is avoided, left out of the town

parts.note: Flint is a town in north Wales
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A man from a Welsh town who has turned down some salad dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing' suggests salad; it is a wound dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lint is a soft linen fabric used for dressing wounds.

clue.text: Insect, bumbling I wager

indicators.note: bumbling means clumsy and muddled, so these letters are confused

explanation.surface: A clumsy insect, someone bets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bumbling' hints at bees but signals the rearranging of I WAGER.
explanation.definitionFit: An earwig is a small insect with pincers at its tail end.

clue.text: District of Paris pulled out of by financial establishment

parts.note: left means departed or pulled out of
a bank is a financial institution

explanation.surface: A Paris district abandoned by a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: The Left Bank is the southern side of the Seine in Paris, famed for artists and students.
